# Recent Hypertension Guidelines

## Key Diagnostic Thresholds

### Major Guidelines (as of my knowledge cutoff)
| Organization | Hypertension Threshold |
|---|---|
| **ACC/AHA (2017)** | ≥130/80 mmHg |
| **ESC/ESH (2018/2023 update)** | ≥140/90 mmHg |
| **JNC 8 (2014)** | ≥140/90 mmHg (≥150/90 for >60 years) |

> **Note:** Guidelines evolve - always verify current versions from professional organizations

---

## Diagnosis

### Measurement Standards
- **Multiple readings** on separate occasions
- Preferred methods: office, home (HBPM), or ambulatory (ABPM) monitoring
- Rule out **white coat hypertension** and **masked hypertension**
- Confirm with out-of-office measurements when possible

### Classification (ACC/AHA 2017)
- **Elevated:** 120-129 / <80
- **Stage 1:** 130-139 / 80-89
- **Stage 2:** ≥140 / ≥90
- **Hypertensive crisis:** >180/>120

---

## Risk Stratification
- Cardiovascular risk calculators (e.g., **ASCVD risk score**)
- Assess for **target organ damage**: LVH, CKD, retinopathy
- Consider secondary causes if indicated

---

## Treatment

### Lifestyle Modifications (All Stages)
- **DASH diet** (reduce sodium to <2.3g/day, ideally <1.5g)
- Weight reduction (5-20 mmHg per 10kg lost)
- Regular aerobic exercise (150+ min/week)
- Limit alcohol
- Smoking cessation

### Pharmacological Therapy

**First-line agents:**
- **ACE inhibitors / ARBs** (especially with diabetes, CKD, proteinuria)
- **Thiazide diuretics** (chlorthalidone preferred over HCTZ in some guidelines)
- **Calcium channel blockers** (dihydropyridines)
- **Beta-blockers** (specific indications: HF, post-MI, certain arrhythmias)

### When to Start Medication
| Guideline | Threshold |
|---|---|
| ACC/AHA | ≥130/80 with high CV risk; ≥140/90 all others |
| ESC/ESH | ≥140/90 (consider earlier with very high risk) |

### Special Populations
- **CKD:** ACE inhibitor or ARB preferred
- **Diabetes:** ACE inhibitor or ARB preferred
- **Heart failure:** ACE inhibitor/ARB + beta-blocker + diuretic
- **Pregnancy:** Labetalol, nifedipine, methyldopa (avoid ACE/ARB)
- **Elderly:** Generally target <130-140 systolic; start low, go slow
- **Resistant hypertension:** Consider aldosterone antagonists (spironolactone), renal denervation

---

## Monitoring & Follow-up
- Reassess 1 month after medication initiation
- Monitor electrolytes, renal function with ACE/ARB + diuretics
- Target BP: generally **<130/80** (ACC/AHA) or **<140/90** (ESC/ESH)

---

## Important Caveats
- ⚠️ Guidelines differ between organizations and are regularly updated
- ⚠️ Always consult **current published guidelines** (ACC, AHA, ESC, WHO)
- ⚠️ Treatment should be **individualized** based on patient comorbidities
- ⚠️ This is **educational information**, not a substitute for clinical judgment

For the most current recommendations, check:
- [ACC/AHA](https://www.acc.org)
- [ESC](https://www.escardio.org)
- [WHO](https://www.who.int)
